note.text: A discussion can describe pressures, explain a possible cause and suggest support without making a diagnosis. Use may or can for possibilities rather than declaring that every teenager has the same experience. A speaker can disagree respectfully and ask for clarification. Use fictional situations; nobody must disclose private experiences. When a problem concerns harm or serious distress, encourage help from a trusted adult or appropriate trained service rather than relying only on classmates.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original dialogue: Bih says an imaginary pupil feels pulled between homework and household duties. Ayuk asks which tasks have fixed deadlines. They suggest discussing a realistic schedule with a responsible adult. Another speaker notes that a schedule may help time pressure but cannot solve every problem. Each turn develops the case without judging the pupil's character.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Separate the difficulty, evidence, possible cause and proposed support. Avoid generalisations such as all teenagers are lazy. Give a reason for a suggestion and recognise its limits. Prepare questions on paper before a partner discussion; the app checks written choices, not spoken performance.
